# Page not found

Last updated: 2026-09-03

## Sorry, that page is not here.

You did not do anything wrong. We may have moved the page you're looking for.

### Did you follow a link from Yukon.ca?

If you reached this page from another part of Yukon.ca, let us know so we can correct our mistake.

Email: [inquiry.desk@yukon.ca](mailto:inquiry.desk@yukon.ca)

Phone: 867-667-5811 or toll free in the Yukon 1-800-661-0408

### Did you follow a link from another site?

Links from other sites can sometimes be old or misspelled. Let us know where you came from and we can try to contact the other site to fix the problem.

Email: [inquiry.desk@yukon.ca](mailto:inquiry.desk@yukon.ca)

Phone: 867-667-5811 or toll free in the Yukon 1-800-661-0408

### Did you type the URL?

You may have typed the address (URL) wrong. Check to make sure you’ve got the exact right spelling or capitalization.

The online daily campground permit is now called the “nightly camping voucher”. - Reserve a site - Changes, cancellations and closures - Park and campground policies Reserve a site ### How to make a reservation Create a [MyYukon](https://yukon.ca/en/your-government/get-government-yukon-online-services-account) account using the "sign in" link at the top of [yukon.goingtocamp.com](https://yukon.goingtocamp.com/). Ensure you sign in before reserving a campsite. Please note: - The reservation holder (“occupant”) you name when booking your reservation must be present upon arrival and throughout the stay. - The reservation holder must also fill out and register a campsite permit upon arrival to the campground. - Reservations are non-transferable to another person or another campground. ### 2026 important dates #### Backcountry campgrounds in [Tombstone Territorial Park](https://yukon.ca/en/outdoor-recreation-and-wildlife/camping/hike-and-camp-tombstone-territorial-park "Hike and camp at Tombstone Territorial Park") | | | | --- | --- | | Reservations open | March 4 at 9 am | | Dates available to reserve | July 1 to September 7 | | Campgrounds with reservable sites | Grizzly Lake
Divide Lake
Talus Lake | #### Frontcountry campgrounds | | | | --- | --- | | Reservations open | April 8 at 9 am | | Dates available to reserve | May 8 to October 1 | | Campgrounds with reservable sites
_(50 per cent of campsites are reservable;_
_50 per cent are first come, first served)_ | [Marsh Lake](https://yukon.ca/en/outdoor-recreation-and-wildlife/camping/site/marsh-lake-campground "Marsh Lake Campground")
[Pine Lake](https://yukon.ca/en/outdoor-recreation-and-wildlife/camping/site/pine-lake-campground "Pine Lake Campground")
[Wolf Creek](https://yukon.ca/en/outdoor-recreation-and-wildlife/camping/site/wolf-creek-campground "Wolf Creek Campground")
[Tombstone Mountain](https://yukon.ca/en/outdoor-recreation-and-wildlife/camping/site/tombstone-mountain-campground "Tombstone Mountain Campground")
[Kusawa Lake](https://yukon.ca/en/outdoor-recreation-and-wildlife/camping/site/kusawa-lake-campground "Kusawa Lake Campground")
[Fox Lake](https://yukon.ca/en/outdoor-recreation-and-wildlife/camping/site/fox-lake-campground "Fox Lake Campground") | ### Fees Payment for your campsite reservation allows you to obtain and register a campsite permit upon arrival in the campground without paying for the permit at the campground.  Payment for each night of your stay at each campsite is required when you make your reservation for each campsite. A campsite permit is still required if you have a reservation. | | | | --- | --- | | Campsite permit, advanced payment | $18 per campsite, per night | | Reservation, backcountry campground | $10 per reservation, in addition to campsite permit fee | | Reservation, frontcountry campground | $0 - no additional reservation fee, only the daily campsite permit fee | - Annual camping voucher holders are able to reserve with their voucher for up to three camping nights per season at frontcountry reservable campgrounds, at no additional cost. - The online reservation system does not support annual camping vouchers as a payment method. - After April 8, 2026, call 867-667-5648 from Monday to Friday between 9 am to 4 pm (YST) to make a booking with an annual camping voucher. Have your environment client ID and your annual camping voucher number ready. - The annual camping voucher cannot be used to reserve backcountry sites. - Yukon residents ages 65 years and over receive a 50% discount on all camping permits. There are no discounts on reservation fees. - A Yukon resident is a person who makes their home, resides and is ordinarily present in the Yukon. ### Self-check-in and register a campsite permit upon arrival You must self-check-in and register your reserved site before 12 pm (noon) on the day after your scheduled arrival date. If you do not arrive and check-in by then, your reservation is cancelled without refund and your site is made available to others. When you arrive at the campground, self-register your reservation and campsite permit: 1. Upon your arrival you must [self check-in online](https://yukon.goingtocamp.com/). 2. Take a green campsite permit. 3. Completely fill out both portions of the permit. 4. Tear off the bottom half of the permit and place it in the deposit vault. 5. Clip the top half of the permit to your reserved campsite post. ### Check-in and check-out times You may arrive any time after 3 pm on the first day of your reservation. Your reservation is held until noon the next day. Once you self-check-in upon arrival, your campsite permit is valid until 12 pm (noon) on your departure day. ### Accessible sites Some campsites available for reservation are designed to be wheelchair accessible. Accessible sites are marked on our [campground maps](https://yukon.ca/en/find-campground-or-recreation-site) with a wheelchair symbol. All barrier-free campsites have a: - level, compacted gravel site surface; - wheelchair-accessible adjustable firepit; and - picnic table with overhanging end for close wheelchair placement. All accessible sites are also close to a wheelchair-accessible outhouse, garbage bin, wood bin and registration kiosk. Some sites have other accessible amenities nearby, such as a kitchen shelter or trail. To camp at an accessible campsite at least one occupant must have a disability that results in them requiring the use of a mobility or visual aid, or the assistance of another person or service animal. ### Special notes for backcountry campgrounds in Tombstone Territorial Park Campsite reservations can be made up to 12 pm (noon) on your day of departure into the backcountry. You can book up to 3 sites, each with a maximum of 2 people. Watch the 10-minute video, [Tombstone Territorial Park Backcountry Orientation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OJm4JWC_csA), prior to your visit. You can also watch it at the [Tombstone Interpretive Centre](https://yukon.ca/en/places/tombstone-interpretive-centre). Check-in and registration are required at the Tombstone Interpretive Centre before entering the backcountry. Be sure to bring the following to register: - Your reservation confirmation letter - All members of your group - Your bear-proof canisters to verify all attractants are stored properly To receive camping permits, all hikers must register in person at the Tombstone Interpretive Centre. Registration times are 9 am, 10 am, 11 am, 12 pm (noon) for same day departures, or 4 pm for next day departures Learn more about [backcountry camping in Tombstone Territorial Park](https://yukon.ca/hike-camp-tombstone#camping-at-tombstone-territorial-park). Changes, cancellations and closures This applies to both frontcountry and backcountry reservations, including standard camping, walk-in tent camping and group camping. ### Changes You can make changes to your frontcountry reservation, free of charge, up until the moment that you self-check-in and register your campsite permit. Once you’ve checked in, changes are no longer possible – only cancellations. If you need to make a change to your backcountry reservation, you must cancel your reservation and start a new booking. Annual camping voucher holders can make changes to their reservation with at least 24 hours notice. It's recommended to make changes at least 3 days in advance to allow other campers the opportunity to use the campsite. Changes can only be made Monday through Friday, between 9 am and 4 pm YST. To make changes to your reservation, call 867-667-5648. ### Cancellations and refunds You can [cancel your reservation online](https://yukon.goingtocamp.com/) or by calling 1-888-352-0532 (toll free) or 1-250-410-0509 (international). Refunds are based on when you cancel, with respect to 12 pm on your scheduled arrival date: | Cancellation made | Refund percentage\* | | --- | --- | | More than 72 hours | 75 | | 24-72 hours | 50 | | Less than 24 hours | 0 - no refund | \*The $10 backcountry campsite reservation fee for Tombstone Territorial Park is non-refundable. Example: You are scheduled to arrive at your reserved campsite on July 10. Refunds would be processed as follows: | If you cancel: | Refund percentage\* | | --- | --- | | _Earlier_ than 12 pm on July 7 | 75 | | _Later_ than 12 pm on July 7
and
_Earlier_ than 12 pm on July 9 | 50 | | _Later_ than 12 pm on July 9 | 0 (no refund) | Annual camping voucher holders are encouraged to cancel reservations at least 3 days in advance to allow other campers the opportunity to use the campsite. Cancellations can only be made Monday through Friday, between 9 am and 4 pm YST. To cancel your reservation, call 867-667-5648. ### No show #### Frontcountry reservations You must self-check-in and register your campsite permit for your reserved campsite before 12 pm (noon) the day after your scheduled arrival date. If you do not arrive and check-in by then, your reservation is considered a no show. The reservation is cancelled without refund and the campsite is made available to others. #### Backcountry reservations All hikers must register in person at the Tombstone Interpretive Centre daily between 9 am and 12 pm (noon) for same day departures, or by 4 pm for next day departures. ### Park and area closures At times, Yukon Parks must close campsites, campgrounds, or parts of campgrounds to ensure visitor safety, protect natural resources or facilities and for other reasons. If Yukon Parks closes a campsite, campground or part of a campground for any reason, all affected reservations will be cancelled immediately. We will do our best to provide you with as much notice as possible in these situations. Refunds for closures will be processed automatically as follows: | Scenario | Refund percentage | | --- | --- | | Camping stay not yet started (you have not checked in and registered yet). | 100 per cent of campground permit fees
0 per cent of backcountry reservation fees | | Camping stay in progress (you have checked in and registered). | 0 per cent - no refund | #### Example: Yukon Parks closes Wolf Creek Campground due to a flooding incident. Parks staff direct all people in the campground to evacuate. All reservations and campsite permits are cancelled immediately. At this point, campers who have checked in and registered their campsite are not eligible for a refund. People who have reservations during the period of the closure, but have not yet arrived and checked in, will automatically get a full refund of all fees paid. People who wish to reserve a campsite after a closure has ended, including those whose reservation was cancelled due to the closure, are required to make a new reservation. ### Special notes for backcountry campgrounds Area closures and advisories can occur with short notice. Check with park staff and any signage at trailheads before heading into the backcountry. Park and campground policies As a reservation holder, you must follow the same rules and guidelines as other park users. These include: - [Rules and safety at campgrounds and recreation sites](https://yukon.ca/en/rules-safety-campgrounds-recreation-sites) - Having a [park permit](https://yukon.ca/en/get-territorial-park-permit) or [wilderness tourism license](https://yukon.ca/en/wilderness-tourism), if you need one - Guidelines for [safe and respectful wilderness travel](https://yukon.ca/en/travel-safely-and-gently-yukon-wilderness) - Guidelines for [Tombstone Territorial Park](https://yukon.ca/en/planning-trip-tombstone-territorial-park) - Posted advisories, such as park closures and fire bans, and other requests by enforcement officers to ensure park protection and public safety In addition, reservation holders must agree to: - park only your camping unit plus a maximum of 2 additional vehicles at your campsite; and - the [change, cancellation and closure policies](https://yukon.ca/en/campsite-reservations#park-and-campground-policies). Previous Next Contact If you have questions, email [yukon.parks@yukon.ca](mailto:yukon.parks@yukon.ca) or phone 867-667-5648. # Get a campsite permit

Last updated: 2026-09-23

Campground permit name changes

The Yukon resident annual campground permit is now called the “annual camping voucher”. The online daily campground permit is now called the “nightly camping voucher”.

You need a campsite permit to register your campsite once you arrive at a Government of Yukon campground.

Permits are available at the information/self-registration kiosks in our [42 road-accessible campgrounds](https://yukon.ca/en/outdoor-recreation-and-wildlife/camping/find-campground-or-recreation-site).

You must register all campsite use – day or night, year-round – using the campsite permit envelopes provided in the campground.

## Who needs a permit

Everyone who uses a campsite within a territorial park needs a campsite permit. This includes road-accessible campgrounds and backcountry campgrounds.

From May 1 through September 30, campsites may only be used for camping. From October 1 through April 30, they may also be used for day use activities. Campsite permits are required for all use year-round.

Check the [current status](https://yukon.ca/en/outdoor-recreation-and-wildlife/camping/find-status-yukon-campgrounds-and-recreation-sites) of campsites, as we may close sites due to flooding, wildlife danger, road conditions or other hazards.

## Permit cost

You can get a campsite permit by paying cash on-site or by:

- purchasing a nightly camping voucher;
- purchasing an annual camping voucher; or
- making a [campsite reservation](https://yukon.ca/en/outdoor-recreation-and-wildlife/camping/campsite-reservations) at 1 of 6 reservable campgrounds.

Fees apply to get a campsite permit from May 1 to September 30. All fees include GST.

- Cash, paid on site: $20
- Nightly camping voucher: $18
- Advanced payment using the [reservation system](https://yukon.ca/en/campsite-reservations): $18
  - An additional $10 service fee applies to backcountry campground reservations
  - Reservations are only available at Marsh Lake, Pine Lake, Tombstone Mountain, Wolf Creek, Fox Lake and Kusawa Lake campgrounds.
- Annual camping voucher (Yukon residents only): $200

Yukon residents ages 65 and over get a 50 per cent discount on all campsite permits, camping vouchers and online reservations.

Annual camping voucher holders are able to reserve with their permit for up to 3 camping nights per season at frontcountry reservable campgrounds, at no additional cost.

- The online reservation system does not support annual camping vouchers as a payment method.
- After April 9, 2025, call 867-667-5648 from Monday to Friday (not open on holidays) between 9 am to 4 pm (YST) to make a booking with an annual camping voucher.
- The annual camping voucher cannot be used to reserve backcountry sites.

## Nightly and annual camping vouchers

Nightly camping vouchers and annual camping vouchers may be purchased at a vendor, [environment office](https://yukon.ca/en/environment-office) or online from April 1 to September 30.

[Get a camping voucher online](https://env.eservices.gov.yk.ca/WebUI/ "Get a camping voucher online")

Nightly camping vouchers expire after 21 days if they are not used. An individual voucher can only be used to pay for 1 night of first-come, first-served camping.

Non-Yukon residents cannot buy or use annual camping vouchers.

Carcross and Tagish campgrounds are not owned or operated by the Government of Yukon. Annual camping vouchers are not accepted at these locations. For more information about fees and payments, contact the Carcross/Tagish First Nation.

## Where to get a campsite permit

In our [42 road-accessible campgrounds](https://yukon.ca/en/outdoor-recreation-and-wildlife/camping/find-campground-or-recreation-site), campsite permits are available at the information kiosks. Campsite permits for backcountry campgrounds in [Tombstone Territorial Park](https://yukon.ca/en/outdoor-recreation-and-wildlife/parks-and-protected-areas/tombstone-territorial-park "Tombstone Territorial Park") can only be obtained at the [Tombstone Interpretive Centre](https://yukon.ca/en/places/tombstone-interpretive-centre "Tombstone Interpretive Centre").

## Register a campsite permit

When you arrive in the campground, find an unoccupied first come, first served campsite or the campsite for which you have a reservation. Next, go to an information kiosk to get your campsite permit and instructions on how to register your permit.

For first come, first served campsites:

1. Take a white campsite permit with attached envelope.
2. Find a campsite. Make sure the site is unoccupied by checking dates on the previous permit, if it's still on the post.
3. Completely fill out the campsite permit and envelope.
4. If paying for your permit with cash, put it in the envelope and seal it.
5. Tear the campsite permit from the envelope and clip it to your campsite number post.
6. Place the envelope in the deposit vault.

For reservable campsites in road accessible campgrounds:

1. Upon your arrival, [check-in online](https://yukon.goingtocamp.com/).
2. Take a green campsite permit.
3. Completely fill out both portions of the permit.
4. Tear off the bottom half of the permit and place it in the deposit vault.
5. Clip the top half of the permit to your reserved campsite post.

For backcountry campgrounds in [Tombstone Territorial Park](https://yukon.ca/en/outdoor-recreation-and-wildlife/parks-and-protected-areas/tombstone-territorial-park "Tombstone Territorial Park"), you must check-in and get your campsite permit in person at the [Tombstone Interpretive Centre](https://yukon.ca/en/places/tombstone-interpretive-centre "Tombstone Interpretive Centre") before entering the backcountry.

## Rules

- You must register and display your campsite permit. Find instructions on how to do this at the information kiosks in the campgrounds.
- Most campsites in road-accessible campgrounds are first come, first served.
- You may not tamper with a valid campsite permit at a site not occupied by yourself.
- You may not obtain and register a campsite permit for anyone other than yourself.
- The camping permit must be registered under the same name as the camping voucher or reservation.

[Learn more about camping rules and safety](https://yukon.ca/en/rules-and-safety-campgrounds-and-recreation-sites)

## Other types of park permits

You may need a different type of park permit depending on the activity you are doing. A park permit is required for certain activities, such as:

- taking-off or landing of an aircraft, and flying a drone;
- commercial filming or photography;
- research and educational activities;
- exploration for or harvesting of natural resources;
- occupation and development of land;
- commercial recreation;
- special events, gatherings or programs; and
- recreational activities by large groups of people.

[Learn more about park permits.](https://yukon.ca/en/doing-business/permits-and-licensing/get-territorial-park-permit)

### Group use area

The Kusawa Lake Campground group use area is available for public use for large gatherings, including overnight camping and day use.

[Learn more or apply for a permit to use the group use area](https://yukon.ca/en/outdoor-recreation-and-wildlife/camping/site/kusawa-lake-campground "Kusawa Lake Campground").
